name: Levomepromazine
metabolism: Evidence is from Levomepromazine Maleate 25 mg tablets (oral). On average 50% of an orally administered dose reached the general circulation as unchanged levomepromazine. The apparent volume of distribution was 23 to 42 L/kg and the biologic half-life 15 to 30 hours. A human study after oral administration found glucuronides, sulfoxide and possibly non-oxidised drug in the urine and non-oxidised drug in the faeces. CYP3A4 is the main isoform responsible for levomepromazine 5-sulfoxidation (72%) and N-demethylation (78%) at a therapeutic concentration of 10 micromolar, with CYP1A2 contributing 20% to 5-sulfoxidation. Excretion is slow, with a half-life of about 30 hours, mainly via urine and faeces; metabolites are eliminated mainly in the urine, and an average 10% of the daily dose was eliminated in urine as levomepromazine sulfoxide.
summary: Levomepromazine, also known as methotrimeprazine, is a phenothiazine neuroleptic and low-potency antipsychotic. Its analgesic, hypnotic, and antiemetic properties are used mainly in palliative care.
